title: Lesson 24: Training the Client's Team to Own the System
description: Training is not handover and not a demo: build operational, change, and sustaining ownership in a small set of named operators, sequence real work from shadowing to solo, build the judgment docs cannot carry, and train the trainer so the capability survives turnover.

questions.question: Per the lesson about training the client's team to own the system, what is the central focus?
options: Building operational, change, and sustaining ownership so named operators can run, change, and teach the system without you
A history of corporate training methods
Instruction on designing slide decks for workshops
A review of project management software
questions.explanation: The lesson defines ownership as three distinct capabilities (run, change, sustain) and teaches training that builds all three.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson's guidance on training versus demonstration?
options: Give a narrated demo so the client watches the system work and feels confident
If you are the one typing, the client is not learning to own it, so keep your hands off the controls and let them do real tasks
Train the whole department at once so everyone gets the overview
Training is the same thing as handing over the operating docs and runbooks
questions.explanation: The lesson's rule is that a training session has the client run the system, read the output, make mistakes, and figure things out while you coach, and never a demo where you carry the work.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support about sustaining the capability over time?
options: Train one highly capable operator and the team is fully self-sufficient
Escalation is a sign of weakness, so operators should improvise on judgment calls
An operator should trust a plausible-looking output over a stated standard such as the golden set
Name at least two operators and train the trainer, so no single person's absence stops the work and the capability survives the first turnover before you leave
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches two operators at the same standard plus a train-the-trainer step, verified by watching the team teach a new member without you, so ownership survives any single person leaving.
